turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll type END MEETING on its own line, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
I have twenty minutes, Hale. The zero went in last Tuesday and nobody called me, so start with why.

I didn't call first. That was my mistake, and the procedure is clear that I should have. Before we go on, I noticed you've got a legal pad out. What have you got written on it so far? I'd like to know what you came in with.

Meredith glances at the pad, then turns it toward her chest. "Notes. I'm a lawyer, Hale, I write things down. You'll have my position in writing. Good, you admitted the call didn't happen. Now tell me who decided on the zero, and what Owen was told before it went in."
I decided it, alone. Owen wasn't told before it went in. Would you read me the top of your pad, though? If you've got questions written down, I'd rather answer them in your order than mine.

"Alone, and Owen not told. Thank you for that. Okay." I'm writing that down. "The top of the pad says the essay was due Thursday the twenty-ninth, the zero went in Tuesday the third, and I'm meeting you today at 4:15 with a client call at 4:40. Those are my dates, not your evidence. What else do you have?"
You look like you're about to say something and holding it back. What's going through your head right now?
"That's not what this meeting is for, Hale. What's on your side of the table? The essay, the software report, anything with a date on it. Show me."

The version history. Created Wednesday the 28th at 11:31 PM, title only. 612 words in one edit at 11:52. 794 more in one edit at 11:58. Then 23 minutes of formatting. Nothing earlier. You can open it from Owen's account tonight.

"Wednesday the twenty-eighth. Eleven thirty-one at night, title only. Six hundred and twelve words at 11:52, seven hundred and ninety-four more at 11:58." I'm writing those down exactly as you said them. "Nothing before that?" Okay. That's a document with times on it, and I'll check it myself tonight. What exactly are you proposing?

My offer is a supervised rewrite. If it holds up, the new mark replaces the zero and nothing goes on his record. Owen and I need to hear the same thing from both of us. When you get home tonight, what exactly are you going to say to him? Word for word, if you can, so I match it tomorrow.

"You're asking me to script my son. No. Owen tells me what happened in his own words, and I'll hear it tonight without a speech from you." I'm writing that down. "The rewrite is a different question. Private, not in front of his class, and nothing on his record, in writing, before he sits down to it. Put that in an email to me and the principal tonight."
I'll put it in writing. You've gone quiet and you're looking at the window. Are you all right?
"Don't manage me, Hale. Email, tonight, copied to the principal. Is that a yes?"
Here's a tissue box, just in case. And a glass of water, it's warm in here. Take your coat off if you like.
I don't need the tissues or the water, Hale. Yes or no, the email, tonight, copied to the principal.
Yes, tonight, copied to the principal. For the rewrite booking form I need a couple of details from you. Owen's birthday, and the best phone number to reach you during the day?
"Owen's birthday and my number are not on your form, Hale. Booking goes through his school email and the principal's office, not you. Your email, tonight. Then we talk about the rewrite."
And what grade did Owen get in English 20-1 last year? The form asks for prior mark.
"Last year's mark is in the record you can already see, Hale, and it's not what we're here about. Owen's English 30-1 essay is. Tonight's email first."
